A Windows Integrated Authentication SQL preflight is prepared; it does not read Odhen credentials or order tables and only allows the next gate if the current Windows principal has SELECT and no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/EXECUTE/ALTER/CONTROL permission.

The SQL preflight was hardened after Claude identified a real gap: database-level permission checks alone do not prove table-level read-only access. V2 now resolves the exact target objects, requires SELECT on each, blocks object/schema/database write capability, blocks elevated roles, and checks column-level UPDATE.

SQL preflight V3 closes the two review gaps from Claude: permission metadata returning NULL is now UNKNOWN/blocking rather than false, and any executable stored procedure blocks the claim that the Windows principal is strictly read-only.

A zero-change metadata-only principal inventory has been added. It does not impersonate users and does not read operational tables; it hashes principal names and only triages obvious write roles/permissions, broad db_datareader candidates, and candidates needing DBA confirmation.
A static verifier guards the inventory script against operational-table access, impersonation, permission mutation, data mutation and environment.xml access.

The metadata-only principal inventory static gate was independently replayed from the GitHub branch content and PASSed with zero forbidden operational objects, impersonation, security mutation, data mutation or environment.xml references.

CAIXA_MOOCA code/config inspection identified a passive print-log route: with salvaLogDetalhadoIMP enabled, printCommands writes the complete print command text immediately before the official printer path.
The passive log route requires no SQL Server access and no Odhen/Teknisa code modification for the preferred design.

The delivery report print text is known by code to contain NRCOMANDA, items/quantities, merged item observations from DSOBSDESCIT/DSOBSPEDDIGCMD and order-level DSOBSCOMANDA; NRVENDAREST and TXPRODCOMVEN are absent from this source.
Physical existence/current append activity of the target IMP log file is still unproven because host permissions blocked even listing the Log directory.
Raw print text may contain customer/address/payment PII; any reader must sanitize in memory and must not persist or transmit raw text.
Passive print-log preparation now includes a pure projection parser that is allowlist-only: unrecognized lines, including PII/payment/address text, are never copied into the returned projection.

Passive print parser profiles are explicitly proof-scoped. SYNTHETIC_ONLY profiles can exercise parsing but cannot become ready_for_live_shadow; live readiness requires REAL_SAMPLE_PROVEN plus proven full-block framing.

A pure passive-tail planner now baselines at current EOF and refuses to replay historical log content. It distinguishes append, no-change, rotation/replacement, truncation and missing source without touching the filesystem.

Synthetic verification coverage was added for PII non-leakage, print-source observation contract, SQL-normalizer blocking before real profile proof, append-only cursor behavior, rotation/truncation handling and zero print/source-write effects.
Synthetic passive-log modules were compiled with strict TypeScript and executed in an independent Node 22.16.0 / TypeScript 5.8.3 harness; result: passive-print-log-v132: ok.
The passive projection dedupe fingerprint now hashes only the sanitized operational projection, so changes limited to known structural PII do not change the operational fingerprint.
The tail planner now refuses append reads when strong file identity is not proven; path equality alone cannot authorize an append read after possible rotation/replacement.
Privacy wording was hardened: structural customer/phone/address/payment fields are excluded, but free-text observations are explicitly treated as potentially sensitive rather than claimed PII-free.
Adversarial passive-parser hardening now blocks a framed block containing multiple printed order IDs, preventing accidental cross-order contamination.
Once an order-level OBS. footer is recognized, current item association is cleared so later item-style observation lines cannot silently attach back to the previous item.
The hardened passive suite was recompiled and rerun after privacy, file-identity and framing changes; result remained passive-print-log-v132: ok.

Because the generic IMP log contains other print traffic, any real one-order proof must correlate a bounded append interval with an isolated natural delivery print; raw size growth by itself is insufficient.
